positive.mainPoint: The following points were well done
subPoints: Good use of NumPy for your homework assignment.
Abbreviation: good job on using use the community abbreviation of `np`.
Types: Good job on ensuring NumPy objects usage.
Functions: Good usage of NumPy functions (e.g., `np.mean`, `np.sqrt`, `np.square`, `np.subtract`, etc.).
Vectorization: Good use of NumPy's vectorization instead of loops (e.g., for loops).
Array Operations: Array reshaping done correctly.
Array Operations: Array slicing and/or filtering done correctly.
Array Operations: Combining arrays done correctly.
Polynomials: Correctly utilized the 'numpy.polynomial.polynomial' module or 'Polynomial.fit'.
Random Number: Very nice application of NumPy's random number generation.
Toy Data: Excellent inclusion of noise into your toy data.
Style: Please use the standard community abbreviation 'import numpy as np'.
Separation of ideas: Consider handling data conversion (e.g., Pandas DataFrame or List to a NumPy array) outside of the core computing function.
Toy Data, Reproducibility: Consider setting a random seed (e.g., np.random.default_rng(seed)) to make your toy data reproducible.
Toy Data, Noise: Consider adding a 'noisy' component to your generated toy data for more realistic simulation.
Performance: the NumPy solution ran slower than expected.
Vectorization: iterating over the NumPy ndarray via a loop defeats the purpose of vectorization and hurts performance.

negative.mainPoint: NumPy Built-ins and Data Type Handling
subPoints: Numpy function was passed/used an incorrect data type (e.g., Pandas DataFrame, List, etc.) instead of a NumPy array.
NumPy Function incorrectly returned (e.g., Floats / Lists / Pandas DataFrames / Other):
Used non-NumPy function or manually calculated math operations instead of using NumPy functions (e.g., np.mean, np.sqrt, np.square, np.subtract, etc.).
Used inefficient standard Python loops to generate random distributions instead of vectorized NumPy random functions.
Polynomial equation usage: The solution failed to use NumPy's 'polynomial.polynomial' or 'Polynomial.fit'.
timeit: Poor or improper usage of the timeit library.
